alerts.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 18 at 2:10PM EST until November 19 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
alerts.description:
* WHAT...East winds 25 to 30 mph with frequent gusts up to 45 mph.

* WHERE...Coastal Broward, Coastal Miami Dade, Coastal Palm Beach,
Metro Broward, Metro Palm Beach, and Metropolitan Miami Dade
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 1 AM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued November 18 at 12:50PM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Far South Miami-Dade County, Inland Broward
County, Inland Miami-Dade County, Inland Palm Beach County, Metro
Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami
Dade.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several rounds of storms may produce rainfall amounts of 2 to 4
inches through late Thursday. Higher amounts of 6 to 8 inches
with locally isolated amounts over 10 inches may be possible.
Heavy rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour may observe

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
100 PM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Off the Southeast U.S. Coast:
A non-tropical low pressure system is expected to form near the 
northern Bahamas by late Friday.  This system could become a 
subtropical or tropical storm while it moves northward or 
northeastward near or offshore of the southeastern U.S. coast 
through the weekend.  Regardless of development, strong winds, 
dangerous surf, and coastal flooding are likely along portions of 
the southeast and mid-Atlantic coasts into early next week.  
Interests along the eastern U.S. coast should monitor the progress 
of this system.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

$$
